newsitem.title: UK: London on track to elect its own mayor in May 2000.
newsitem.headline: London on track to elect its own mayor in May 2000.

text.p: The new Labour government said on Wednesday it would legislate for a referendum on establishing a new strategic authority for London and a directly elected mayor for the capital.
The bill is part of Prime Minister Tony Blair's election pledge to decentralise power.
It said it would produce a consultation paper this summer so that Londoners and interested organisations can contribute their views. Detailed proposals would be published around Christmas.

Following enactment of the legislation, the referendum would be held in May 1998 and, assuming a "yes" vote, would be followed by further legislation to establish an authority and elected mayor in the second session of parliament.
This should enable elections to take place in May 2000, it said.
London, exceptionally for a metropolis, has been without a city-wide authority since the previous Conservative government abolished the Greater London Council in the 1980s.
